newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Luz del Sur stake seen attractively priced.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Luz del Sur stake seen attractively priced.

text.p: Despite heavy investor interest both home and abroad, the Peruvian government has set an attractive price for its sale of a 30 percent stake in electricity distributor Luz del Sur, local brokers and analysts said.
"The price is excellent for the investor," said Luis Calderon, of Acciones y Valores brokerage. "We can say that the placement has been a success."
After all-night negotiations, privatization officials announced Wednesday morning a price of 3.10 soles ($1.20) per share for the sale of 148.4 million shares in Luz del Sur.
"The truth is that we are a bit surprised," said Emilio Paez, of Helvetia brokerage. "The price is below what was expected, which was around 3.30 soles to 3.40 soles."
Luz del Sur's stock was trading at 3.29 soles at 1000 local time (1000 EST) on the Lima Stock Exchange.
Paez added that Luz del Sur had healthy growth prospects, and investors should see significant profits in coming months on the local market.

Analysts said local individual investors, who have a 10 percent discount on the share's purchase price through the government's Citizens' Participation in Privatization Program, should be delighted at the price.
Manuel Bustamante, of Cruz Blanca, agreed that the sale price was lower than expected and predicted the new holders of company stock would see early profits on the local market.
"We thought the price would be set at 3.20 soles per share. Luz del Sur should shoot up on the bolsa," he said.
The electricity utility sale comes at a time when investors are disappointed with the economy's recent slow growth.

However, in the last few months, utility stocks on the Lima bolsa have consistently outperformed the market, and analysts say the electricity sector has strong growth potential for the medium- and long-term.
The Luz del Sur offer has brought strong demand from within Peru, where the sale to individuals has drawn offers worth 600 million soles ($233 million), meaning unsatisfied demand is inevitable.

Electricity consumption in the Luz del Sur service area in central, eastern and southern Lima rose 9.3 percent to 1.6 million megawatt hours in the first half of 1996, compared to the same period last year. Luz del Sur plans to invest $170 million over the next five years mainly to expand the distributor's service to supply more customers.

The government intends to place all of its 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur, and is scheduled to define the precise distribution of the shares between the local and foreign tranches of the sale in the next few days.

However, privatization officials said the final distribution of shares would probably be changed to sell 60 percent of the government's 30 percent stake through the Citizens' Participation program, rather than the original maximum of 55 percent.
The remaining 40 percent of the government's 30 percent stake will go to Peruvian and foreign institutional investors, where, officials say, demand has also been high.

The former state-run electricity company was privatized in June 1994 when a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc bought a 60 percent stake for $212.1 million. Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.

"I do not have precise figures of foreign demand, but I can say there is a lot of interest, and the amount of shares allocated is far more than covered by demand," said one official, who asked not to be named.

The Luz del Sur sale is seen as Peru's most important share placement since July's successful $1.25 billion placement of a 26.6 percent state-owned share in telecommunications company Telefonica del Peru. -- Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134
